welcome: Welcome to {club}. The board expect a {expectation}-place finish or better. Your deal runs {years} years at £{salary}m a season.
The chairman of {club} shakes your hand: {years} years, £{salary}m a season, and a target of {expectation}. Don't make him regret it.
review_beat: Season over. You finished {finish} against a target of {expectation}. The board are pleased, and the target moves to {finish}.
{finish}, when {expectation} would have done. The board's letter is warm; next year they will want {finish} again.
review_met: Season over. {finish}, as asked. The board note it and say nothing more.
review_missed: Season over. {finish} against a target of {expectation}. The board's letter is short.
The board wanted {expectation} and got {finish}. Their statement thanks the players.
target: The board have set this season's target: {to}.
mood_secure: The board are content. No note this month.
mood_settled: A quiet month from the board.
mood_uneasy: The chairman has asked to see you. {position}, with {expectation} expected, is not what he had in mind.
A note from the board: results must improve. You sit {position}.
mood_under review: Your position is under review. The board meet weekly and your name is on the agenda.
The board have stopped returning calls. {position} is not going to be tolerated much longer.
mood_on the brink: One more result like the last and you will not be here for the next.
sacked_deserved: The board have relieved you of your duties at {club}. Few will argue. You leave with £{payout}m of your contract paid up.
{club} have parted company with you. After the run you have had, the statement is brief. Payout: £{payout}m.
sacked_unjust: {club} have sacked you. The press call it harsh; the board call it a decision. £{payout}m follows you out.
A short meeting at {club} and it is over. Even the players look surprised. Payout: £{payout}m.
mutual: You and {club} have parted by mutual consent. Half your contract, £{payout}m, and a handshake.
resigned: You have resigned from {club}. No payout; the board wish you well in a single sentence.
renewed: {club} have extended your contract: {years} more years at £{salary}m a season.
released: {club} have let your contract run out. The board thank you for your service and mean about half of it.
left: You have chosen not to renew at {club}. You leave at the end of the contract, with nothing owed and no hard feelings.
takeover: {club} have new owners: {to} by all accounts. Whether they want their own man is not yet clear.
crisis: The accountants have been in. Next summer's budget is cut hard; the board have eased your target to {expectation}.
star_sale: The board have sold your best player to balance the books. They have eased the target to {expectation} by way of apology.
row: A row with the board over selection has leaked. It will not have helped.
promoted: Promotion. {club} go up to tier {toTier}. The champagne is the board's; the target next season will be theirs too.
relegated: Relegation. {club} go down to tier {toTier}. The board's statement talks of a fresh start.
trophy: {club} have won the {competition}. Whatever else happens, that is on your record.
career_over: The phone has stopped ringing. After {games} games, £{earnings}m and {trophyPoints} trophy points, the career is over: {reason}.
career_over_voluntary: You have called it a day on your own terms. {games} games, £{earnings}m and {trophyPoints} trophy points go on the record.
career_over_no-offers: Two years without a shortlist. The phone has stopped ringing. After {games} games, £{earnings}m and {trophyPoints} trophy points, the career is over.
career_over_age: The years have done what no chairman managed. After {games} games, £{earnings}m and {trophyPoints} trophy points, you retire.
career_over_scandal: No club will touch you now. After {games} games, £{earnings}m and {trophyPoints} trophy points, the career is over.
